title: "Bike-Share Demand Analysis"
author: "Alli Oluwagbenga"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
# Load the package and read the CSV
library(readr)

bike_day <- read_csv(
  "Bike Share Demand Analysis/day.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Make a copy for analysis
bike <- bike_day

# Create readable month names
month_names <- c(
  "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
  "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"
)

bike$month_name <- factor(
  bike$mnth,
  levels = 1:12,
  labels = month_names
)

# Create readable season names
bike$season <- factor(
  bike$season,
  levels = 1:4,
  labels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
)

# Create readable weather names
bike$weather <- factor(
  bike$weathersit,
  levels = 1:3,
  labels = c(
    "Clear or partly cloudy",
    "Mist or cloudy",
    "Rain, snow or storms"
  )
)
```

```{r}
# Calculate the values used by the charts
average_by_month <- tapply(bike$cnt, bike$month_name, mean)
average_by_season <- tapply(bike$cnt, bike$season, mean)
rider_totals <- c(
  Casual = sum(bike$casual),
  Registered = sum(bike$registered)
)
average_by_weather <- tapply(bike$cnt, bike$weather, mean)
```

```{r}
# Chart 1: Average rentals by month
barplot(
  average_by_month[month.abb],
  names.arg = month.abb,
  main = "Average Bike Rentals by Month",
  xlab = "Month",
  ylab = "Average rentals per day",
  col = "steelblue"
)

# Chart 2: Average rentals by season
barplot(
  average_by_season,
  main = "Average Bike Rentals by Season",
  xlab = "Season",
  ylab = "Average rentals per day",
  col = "steelblue"
)

# Chart 3: Total rentals by rider type
barplot(
  rider_totals,
  main = "Total Rentals by Rider Type",
  xlab = "Rider type",
  ylab = "Total rentals",
  col = "steelblue"
)

# Chart 4: Average rentals by weather
barplot(
  average_by_weather,
  horiz = TRUE,
  las = 1,
  main = "Average Bike Rentals by Weather",
  xlab = "Average rentals per day",
  col = "steelblue"
)
```
